clue.text: Female paragon

definitions.meaning: a model of excellence, a gem of a person

explanation.definitionFit: Pearl is a girl's name, and a pearl is figuratively a thing or person of supreme worth.

clue.text: Stony? Sulk if one is in debt

parts.note: a pet is a fit of sulking

indicators.note: the letters for 'if one' sit inside the word for debt

parts.note: being in debt is being in the red
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A sulker whose finances have gone into the red is stony broke.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags 'Stony' as a looser sense: turned to stone, or frozen with fear.
explanation.definitionFit: Petrified literally means converted into stone, and figuratively rigid with terror.

clue.text: Gather together in a celebration

parts.note: Mass is a celebration of the Eucharist

explanation.surface: People gather at a festive occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to accumulate or collect a great quantity.

clue.text: One can see what the speaker's expressing

definitions.text: One can see what the speaker's expressing

parts.words: One can see what the speaker's expressing
parts.note: seeing rather than hearing words points to someone who follows speech by watching the mouth

explanation.definitionFit: A lip-reader understands speech from the movements of the speaker's mouth.

clue.text: Got together and made score of nineteen, say

definitions.meaning: gathered in, as cattle or suspects are
turned a figure such as 19 into the next ten, 20

explanation.definitionFit: To round up is both to herd people together and to raise a number to the nearest ten.

clue.text: Not a maiden to knock down?

definitions.meaning: in cricket a maiden is an over with no runs scored, so its opposite is an over yielding runs

explanation.definitionFit: In cricket an over scoring runs is not a maiden; a car that knocks down a pedestrian runs them over.

clue.text: What's heard in Security Council is flawed

parts.note: the Security Council is part of the UN, the United Nations
a sound is anything heard

explanation.surface: Something overheard in a UN chamber turns out to be faulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsound means defective or unreliable, not solid.

clue.text: Such a treat isn't really for the wife

definitions.text: Such a treat isn't really for the wife

parts.words: Such a treat isn't really for the wife
parts.note: a treat where each pays their own share is no treat at all; and in Cockney slang 'my old' plus this word means my wife

explanation.definitionFit: A Dutch treat is an outing where everyone pays for themselves, so nobody is truly treated.

clue.text: A certain person's opinions

parts.note: 'certain' means convinced rather than particular: the views of someone utterly sure of themselves

explanation.definitionFit: Dogmatism is the stating of opinions as if beyond question.

clue.text: Change to author church supports

indicators.note: in a down clue the church sits beneath the author word, holding it up

parts.note: to pen is to write, so a pen stands for the author
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A writer proposes changes that the church endorses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' is the noun, coins: pence are small change.
explanation.definitionFit: Pence are the coins that make up loose cash.

clue.text: Cornering with second gear, having the usual accessories

parts.note: cornering a quarry is trapping it

explanation.surface: A driver takes a corner in second gear, with the car fully kitted out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gear' reads as the car's gear but sits with the definition as a second sense: trappings are gear, the usual accessories.
explanation.definitionFit: Trappings are the outward fittings and ornaments that customarily go with something.

clue.text: Catching game, about to follow cross beast

indicators.note: the word for about comes after the game in the answer

parts.note: tig is the British playground chasing game, also called tag
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: Someone playing a chasing game is about to follow an angry animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like 'angry' but means hybrid: a tigon is bred from a tiger and a lioness.
explanation.definitionFit: A tigon is a hybrid offspring of a male tiger and a female lion.

clue.text: One son and girl in family

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
Sue is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A family has one son and a daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'family' here means offspring, the sense in 'died without issue'.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is a legal and formal word for a person's children or descendants.

clue.text: Condescend to hide old brooch in very secure place

indicators.note: the brooch word goes inside the letters for very secure place

parts.note: a safe is a locked box for valuables
ouch is an archaic word for a clasp or brooch

explanation.surface: Someone deigns to hide an antique brooch in a strongbox.
explanation.walkthrough: OUCH, an old word for a jewelled clasp, is the obscure piece; 'to hide' simply links the definition to the instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: To vouchsafe is to grant something graciously, as if stooping from a higher position.

clue.text: Attacker initially driven off, regrouping?

indicators.note: the letters are gathered again in a new order, like troops reforming
the opening letter of the word Attacker is taken

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An assailant, beaten back at first, rallies for another go.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: A (Attacker's first letter) plus DRIVEN, rearranged by 'regrouping'.
explanation.definitionFit: An invader is a force that enters territory to attack it.

clue.text: Little girl's sort of upper-class, having noble rank

parts.note: Vi is a short girl's name, here possessive
county is British slang for belonging to the landed gentry

explanation.surface: A small girl has a slightly posh air and a title.
explanation.definitionFit: A viscounty is the title or rank held by a viscount.

clue.text: Tonic I'd brewed, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: brewing mixes ingredients up, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the apostrophe is dropped, leaving the letters I and D

explanation.surface: A drink mixer has been made up, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a manner of speaking' looks like a throwaway phrase; 'in a' links and 'manner of speaking' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Diction is the style of enunciation in speaking or singing.

clue.text: Priest removing one article from tabernacle, possibly

indicators.note: the remaining letters may be arranged another way

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A priest carries one item out of the tabernacle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing' tells you to take A out of TABERNACLE; the remaining letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrant is the priest who officiates at Mass or a sacrament.

clue.text: Bad reputation, one I try to change

indicators.note: the letters are to be altered in order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is trying to shake off a bad name.
explanation.definitionFit: Notoriety is fame for something unfavourable.

clue.text: She takes Tennessee's so-called transport, heading East

parts.note: Tennessee Williams wrote A Streetcar Named Desire, so the transport is named Desire

indicators.note: the first letter of the word East leads the way

explanation.surface: A woman boards the famous streetcar of Tennessee Williams's play and rides east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' is the definition: Désirée is a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Désirée is a French-derived female forename, meaning desired.

clue.text: Audible range being talked about?

definitions.meaning: the distance within which a sound can be heard
the saying is that your ears burn when others discuss you

explanation.definitionFit: Earshot is hearing distance; read as ears hot, it suggests burning ears from gossip.

clue.text: Pacific tribesmen pass round this

parts.note: 'Pacific' means peace-making rather than the ocean: Native American men share a ceremonial pipe to seal peace

explanation.definitionFit: A calumet is a Native American ceremonial tobacco pipe, smoked as a token of peace.

clue.text: Man from one city caught girl in another

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
Hester is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A man from one town catches a girl in another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man from one city' sets the scene; 'another' is the definition, another city, Chester in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Chester is a cathedral city in Cheshire, England.

clue.text: May possibly give old character to great actor

indicators.note: the actor is attached after the character, in that order

parts.note: thorn is an Old English letter, a character no longer used
Sir Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a celebrated Victorian actor-manager

explanation.surface: A request that an elderly role be handed to a star performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' is not the verb but the hawthorn blossom; 'possibly' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawthorn, a thorn tree, is commonly called may after the month it flowers.

clue.text: Author playing part in Hamlet

indicators.note: only a part of the words Author playing is taken

explanation.surface: A writer is acting a role in Shakespeare's tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamlet' is not the play but a small village.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorp is an archaic word for a village.

clue.text: Girl's name, as usual, left off the end

indicators.note: the letter is dropped from the final position of the word

parts.note: normal means usual or ordinary

explanation.surface: A girl's name, as is customary, is left off the end of a list.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is a female forename.

clue.text: Tradesman who vanished in agony

parts.note: Lewis Carroll subtitled The Hunting of the Snark 'An Agony in Eight Fits'; the bread-making member of the crew softly and suddenly vanishes away

explanation.definitionFit: The Baker is the character in Carroll's Snark who meets a Boojum and disappears.

clue.text: Trick can upset kings extremely

indicators.note: the kings stand at the extremes, one at each end

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king, two of them here

indicators.note: in a down clue the word can is turned upside down

explanation.surface: A trick tin knocks over monarchs.
explanation.definitionFit: A knack is a skill or trick of doing something deftly.

clue.text: One has to admit the monarch

parts.note: to own is to confess, as in own up
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone is obliged to let the sovereign in.
explanation.definitionFit: An owner is the person who possesses something.

clue.text: List of successes in dismantling apartheid

indicators.note: taking something apart lets its letters be rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: Ending apartheid ranks among the great achievements.
explanation.definitionFit: The hit parade is a chart ranking the best-selling popular records.

clue.text: He hands out money to put on pitch a great player

parts.note: to pay a ship's seams is to coat them with pitch or tar
a master is a supreme performer, as at chess

explanation.surface: A club treasurer pays a star to take the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' suggests a sports field, but it is tar: PAY is an old nautical verb for daubing with pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A paymaster is the official who issues wages.

clue.text: Wine's taste initially acceptable

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word taste is used

parts.note: okay means satisfactory

explanation.surface: A wine's flavour is passable at first sip.
explanation.definitionFit: Tokay is a sweet dessert wine from Hungary.
